chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from Manṣūr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

When Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام descended with the adhān upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, his head was in the lap of ʿAlī عليه السلام. So Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام gave the adhān and the iqāmah. Then when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله awoke, he said, “O ʿAlī, did you hear?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Did you memorize?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Call Bilāl and teach him.” So ʿAlī عليه السلام called Bilāl and taught him.

key_terms.أَقَامَ: he gave the iqāmah, the call commencing the prayer
key_terms.بِلَالًا: Bilāl, whom ʿAlī عليه السلام was instructed to teach
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, the angel who brought the adhān
key_terms.حَجْرِ: lap, indicating the Messenger’s resting position with ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.حَفِظْتَ: did you memorize, referring to preserving the wording exactly

ai.seo_question: How was the adhān taught to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and what was the role of ʿAlī عليه السلام in transmitting it?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام brought the adhān and iqāmah to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, while ʿAlī عليه السلام was present and attentive. It highlights the divinely taught origin of the call to prayer and ʿAlī’s عليه السلام direct role in preserving and transmitting it to Bilāl.
